title: Battery bioleaching: methods, conditions and outputs

steps.title: Separate the treatment routes
steps.question: Which treatment routes were identified?
steps.look: Discovery lists one-step, two-step, spent-medium, chemical-leaching and control routes. Section 2.5 describes the three fungal approaches.
steps.boundary: Processes remain flat. A route name alone does not describe its full experimental Setting.

steps.title: Read the one-step setting
steps.question: When do the spores and battery powder meet?
steps.look: Spores enter medium already containing battery powder. The Setting records 100 mL, 1% (w/v), pH 6, 130 rpm, 30 °C and 30 days.
steps.boundary: A Setting supplies experimental context; it is not a recovery measurement.

steps.title: Separate pre-culture from leaching
steps.question: What does the 27-day duration cover?
steps.look: The two-step Setting records 3 days of pre-culture followed by 27 days of leaching. Powder is added after fungal growth begins.
steps.boundary: Pre-culture and powder-contact time are different intervals, not one interchangeable duration.

steps.title: Distinguish cell-free spent medium
steps.question: Are live spores present during leaching?
steps.look: The Setting records cell-free medium: 14 days of cultivation, then 16 days of leaching. Section 2.5 describes filtration before powder addition.
steps.boundary: The stored evidence hint is not verbatim in today's text. Approximate navigation requires selection and does not verify the quotation.

steps.title: Check the actual revision status
steps.question: What was actually committed before Scope and final export?
steps.look: The log shows 17 inherited settings, zero LLM calls and zero applied operations. Process Revision was skipped and not committed.
steps.boundary: Enabled does not mean executed. Setting inheritance is not evidence of an LLM repair.

steps.title: Attach scope: identify the battery batch
steps.question: What was treated?
steps.look: After document merge and revision, Scope adds source context. Scope describes spent lithium-ion phone batteries collected from markets. The experimental section explains their preparation into powder.
steps.boundary: This is a batch, not a handset model. Powder is a preparation form, not a new product identity. Scope is post-merge provenance, not an upstream extraction input.

steps.title: Attach the one-step Li result
steps.question: Which treatment produced this 100% Li result?
steps.look: One-step bioleaching → HAS_OUTPUT → Li reports 100%, linked to the 30-day Setting. The source sentence is highlighted.
steps.boundary: This is a leaching outcome, not battery composition. The value retains its experimental context.

steps.title: Keep the second 100% Li result separate
steps.question: Do equal percentages imply a duplicate observation?
steps.look: Two-step bioleaching also reports 100% Li, but with a different Process and Setting: 27 days after 3 days of pre-culture.
steps.boundary: Equal values do not erase different treatments. These observations are not merged into one unconditional result.

steps.title: Keep the spent-medium result separate
steps.question: Where does the 95% Li result belong?
steps.look: Spent-medium bioleaching reports 95% Li with its own Setting. The sentence also reports other metals as separate output observations.
steps.boundary: Sharing a Li node does not make observations interchangeable. No pooled recovery is computed.

steps.title: Explore the Process bridge
steps.question: Does graph evidence retain its context?
steps.look: Inspect spent-medium bioleaching's inputs and outputs. The Li observation keeps 95% and its conditions; View evidence in replay returns to the source.
steps.boundary: This frozen graph does not transfer recovery rates between treatments or papers.
